extracted.intended_audience: registrants, issuers, sponsors, general partners, and qualified persons preparing SEC Regulation S‑K disclosures (U.S. public company filings)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulation S‑K filing requirements and content standards for SEC disclosures including technical report summaries for mineral projects, exhibits (Interactive Data Files, asset files), recent sales/use of proceeds, purchases of equity securities, and roll-up transaction supplements and summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental studies, permitting, and plans, negotiations, or agreements with local individuals or groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the factors pertaining to environmental compliance, permitting, and local individuals or groups, which are related to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (i) results of environmental studies (e.g., environmental baseline studies or impact assessments); (ii) requirements and plans for waste and tailings disposal, site monitoring, and water management during operations and after mine closure; (iii) project permitting requirements, status of permit applications, and any known requirements to post performance or reclamation bonds; (iv) plans, negotiations, or agreements with local individuals or groups; (v) mine closure plans, including remediation and reclamation plans, and associated costs; (vi) the qualified person's opinion on the adequacy of current plans to address issues related to environmental compliance, permitting, and local individuals or groups; and (vii) descriptions of any commitments to ensure local procurement and hiring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital and operating costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide estimates of capital and operating costs, with major components set out in tabular form and justification of the basis for estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain and justify basis for cost estimates including any contingency budgets; state the accuracy level of estimates. The qualified person must assess risks associated with engineering estimation methods and consider accuracy of those methods in prior similar environments. The accuracy of estimates must comply with §229.1302 (Item 1302 of Regulation S‑K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe key assumptions, parameters, and methods used to demonstrate economic viability and disclose results of economic analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all material assumptions (discount rates, exchange rates, commodity prices, taxes, royalties, and other levies), annual cash flow forecasts based on an annual production schedule for life of project, measures such as NPV, IRR, and payback period. Include sensitivity analysis variants (commodity price, grade, capital and operating costs, or other inputs) and discuss impact. In an initial assessment, an economic analysis is optional; if included, include a statement (equal prominence) that mineral resources do not have demonstrated economic viability. Inferred mineral resources may be included only if conditions in §229.1302(d)(4)(ii) are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjacent properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for including information concerning an adjacent property in the technical report summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A qualified person may include adjacent-property information only if: (i) it was publicly disclosed by the owner/operator of the adjacent property; (ii) the source is identified; (iii) the qualified person states inability to verify the information and that it is not necessarily indicative of mineralization on the subject property; and (iv) the technical report summary clearly distinguishes adjacent-property information from information about the subject property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other relevant data and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include additional information or explanation necessary to provide a complete and balanced presentation of the value of the property to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information included must comply with §§229.1300 through 229.1305 (subpart 229.1300). Use this item to ensure completeness and balance beyond the prescribed items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified person must summarize interpretations and conclusions based on the data and analysis in the technical report summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also discuss any significant risks and uncertainties that could reasonably be expected to affect reliability or confidence in exploration results, mineral resource or reserve estimates, or projected economic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe recommendations for additional work, if applicable, with associated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the additional work program is divided into phases, provide costs for each phase along with decision points at the end of each phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: References
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a list of all references cited in the technical report summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references in sufficient detail so that a reader can locate each reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on information provided by the registrant
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on information provided by the registrant for matters discussed in the technical report summary, provide required disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying as permitted under §229.1302(f), provide the disclosure required pursuant to §229.1302(f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy relating to recovery of erroneously awarded compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant with a class of securities listed on a national securities exchange or association must file its compensation recovery policy as an exhibit to its annual report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the compensation recovery policy required by applicable listing standards adopted pursuant to 17 CFR 240.10D-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports, opinions, or appraisals in de‑SPAC transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities to be registered will be issued in a de‑SPAC transaction, include required reports/opinions/appraisals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all reports, opinions, or appraisals required to be filed or included by §229.1607(c) (Item 1607(c) of Regulation S‑K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for filing any additional exhibits the registrant wishes to file and filing of certain earnings statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Mark additional exhibits clearly to indicate subject matters; (ii) If an issuer makes generally available an earnings statement covering at least 12 months beginning after the effective date by 'other methods' than specified in §230.158, it must be filed as an exhibit to the Form 10‑Q or Form 10‑K covering the period in which the statement was released. Ensure exhibits are filed as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive Data File submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and permissions for submitting an Interactive Data File (XBRL) when financial statements are prepared in accordance with US GAAP or IFRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Interactive Data File (§232.11) is: (i) Required to be submitted to the Commission as provided by §232.405 if the registrant is not registered under the Investment Company Act, except: (A) first required for periodic reports on Form 10‑Q, Form 20‑F, or Form 40‑F as applicable; (B) required for a registration statement under the Securities Act only if the registration statement contains a price or price range; (C) required for Form 8‑K only in specified circumstances (revised audited annual financial statements or disclosure required by Item 1.05(b) of Form 8‑K); (D) required in any filing excluded by certain subparagraphs that contains disclosure required by subpart 229.1600 but only as to such disclosure. (ii) Permitted to be submitted to the Commission in the manner provided by §232.405 if the registrant is not registered under the Investment Company Act and the Interactive Data File is not required under paragraph (i). Instruction: When submitted as provided by §232.405(a)(3)(i), the exhibit index must include the word 'Inline' within the title description for any XBRL-related exhibit. (iii) Not permitted to be submitted if the registrant is registered under the Investment Company Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset Data File
rubrics_metrics.description: An Asset Data File as defined in §232.11 filed pursuant to Item 1111(h)(3) of Regulation AB (§229.1111(h)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the Asset Data File when required by the cited Regulation AB provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset related document
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional asset-level information or explanatory language pursuant to Item 1111(h)(4) and (5) of Regulation AB (§229.1111(h)(4) and (h)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supplemental asset-level disclosures as required by Regulation AB cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Page Interactive Data File
rubrics_metrics.description: A Cover Page Interactive Data File as required by Rule 406 of Regulation S‑T and defined in §232.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and submit the Cover Page Interactive Data File in the manner provided by the EDGAR Filer Manual and Rule 406 of Regulation S‑T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static pool disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Static pool disclosure requirement when not included in the prospectus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not included in the prospectus filed under §230.424(b)(2) or (5) and (h), provide static pool disclosure as required by §229.1105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee table
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing fee table and related disclosure required by specified Form items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the filing fee table and related disclosure as required by §232.408 (Rule 408 of Regulation S‑T). Specific cross-references to many Form items are provided; conform to the submission rules and exceptions noted in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent sales of unregistered securities; use of proceeds from registered securities (Item 701)
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish detailed information as to all securities sold by the registrant within the past three years that were not registered under the Securities Act, including use of proceeds information for registered securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (a) Securities sold — date, title, and amount; (b) Underwriters and other purchasers — names of principal underwriters or class of persons for non-public offerings; (c) Consideration — aggregate offering price and underwriting discounts/commissions for cash sales, or nature and aggregate amount of consideration if non-cash; (d) Exemption from registration claimed — indicate section/rule and briefly state facts relied upon; (e) Terms of conversion or exercise — if presented on certain forms and securities are convertible/exchangeable disclose terms; (f) Use of proceeds — as required by §230.463, report use of proceeds on first periodic report after registration and thereafter until proceeds applied or offering terminated; when disclosing use of proceeds include: (1) effective date and Commission file number; (2) offering date or explanation if not commenced; (3) explanation if offering terminated before sales; (4) if offering did not terminate before sales, disclose (i) whether offering terminated and if before sale of all securities, (ii) managing underwriter names, (iii) title of each class registered, (iv) for each class provide amount registered, aggregate price registered, amount sold and aggregate offering price sold (issuer and selling holders), (v) expenses incurred and whether estimates provided instead of actuals and whether payments were to insiders/affiliates or others, (vi) net offering proceeds, (vii) amounts of net proceeds used for various purposes (construction, purchases, acquisitions, debt repayment, working capital, temporary investments, other uses over threshold) and whether estimates are provided, with indication if payments were to insiders/affiliates or others, and (viii) if use of proceeds represents material change from prospectus, describe briefly. Instructions: short-term instruments maturing within a year may be omitted; totals/periods may be used for series; disclose all purchases covered by Item, including those not meeting safe harbor §240.10b-18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indemnification of directors and officers (Item 702)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the general effect of any statute, charter provision, by-law, contract or other arrangement under which controlling persons, directors or officers are insured or indemnified against liability incurred in their capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise statement of the general effect of the indemnification/insurance arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchases of equity securities by the issuer and affiliated purchasers (Item 703)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide, in the specified tabular format, information for any purchases made by or on behalf of the issuer or any 'affiliated purchaser' of shares or other units of any class of the issuer's equity securities registered under Section 12 of the Exchange Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the table with columns: Period; Total number of shares (or units) purchased; Average price paid per share (or unit); Total number purchased as part of publicly announced plans or programs; Maximum number (or approximate dollar value) that may yet be purchased under plans/programs. For each month in the period disclose the information. Include all issuer repurchases (publicly announced and not); by footnote disclose number purchased other than through publicly announced plans and nature of transaction (e.g., open-market, tender offers, satisfaction of put options). Instructions to (b)(3) and (b)(4): disclose aggregate info for all plans/programs and, by footnote, indicate date each plan was announced, dollar/share amount approved, expiration date (if any), plans expired during the period, plans terminated early or under which issuer does not intend to make further purchases. Instruction: Disclose all purchases covered by this Item, including purchases that do not satisfy the conditions of the safe harbor of §240.10b-18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securities Act industry guides (Subpart 229.800)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of Securities Act industry guides and their topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified guides include: Guide 4 — Prospectuses relating to interests in oil and gas programs; Guide 5 — Preparation of registration statements relating to interests in real estate limited partnerships; Guide 6 — Disclosures concerning unpaid claims and claim adjustment expenses of property-casualty insurance underwriters. (Other paragraphs reserved.) Use the appropriate guide for industry-specific prospectus/disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange Act industry guides (Subpart 229.802)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of Exchange Act industry guides and their topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified guide: Guide 4 — Disclosures concerning unpaid claims and claim adjustment expenses of property-casualty underwriters. (Other paragraphs reserved.) Refer to these guides for Exchange Act disclosure specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — General partner (Item 901(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'general partner' for the purposes of subpart 229.900.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General partner means the person or persons responsible under state law for managing or directing the management of the business and affairs of a partnership that is the subject of a roll-up transaction including, but not limited to, the general partner(s), board of directors, board of trustees, or other person(s) having a fiduciary duty to such partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Partnership and 'finite-life' (Item 901(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'partnership' and the concept of 'finite-life' for roll-up transactions and lists exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnership means any finite-life limited partnership or other finite-life entity. 'Finite-life' (except as noted) means an entity that operates as a conduit vehicle for investors to participate in ownership of assets for a limited period and has a policy/purpose of distributing proceeds from sale/financing/refinancing or cash from operations rather than reinvesting. A real estate investment trust as defined in I.R.C. section 856 is not finite-life solely because of distribution of net income if its policies do not include distribution of proceeds from sale/financing/refinancing. 'Partnership' excludes entities registered under the Investment Company Act or any Business Development Company as defined in that Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Roll-up transaction (Item 901(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'roll-up transaction' and lists transactions that are not included in the definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roll-up transaction means a transaction involving the combination or reorganization of one or more partnerships in which some or all investors will receive new securities or securities in another entity (with enumerated exceptions, e.g., transactions where all interests are repurchased or exchanged per preexisting agreement to a specifically identified operating company; transactions where issued/exchanged securities are not required to be registered; transactions involving issuers not required to register or report under Section 12; certain transactions where a non‑affiliated party succeeds to interests and approvals/compensation conditions are met; transactions meeting specified reporting-plan conditions and numerical limits; transactions not involving significant adverse changes to investors; transactions providing all investors option to receive/retain security under substantially same terms). The Commission may exempt by rule or order any security, transaction, or person from the definition/requirements if consistent with public interest and investor protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Sponsor (Item 901(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'sponsor' for roll-up transaction purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor means the person proposing the roll-up transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Successor (Item 901(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'successor' in the context of a roll-up transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successor means the surviving entity after completion of the roll-up transaction or the entity whose securities are being offered or sold to, or acquired by, limited partners of the partnerships or the limited partnerships to be combined or reorganized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to Item 901 — Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction that the requirements of subpart 229.900 apply to each entity proposed to be included in a roll-up transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a transaction is a roll-up as defined in Item 901(c), the requirements of the subpart apply to each entity proposed for inclusion, whether or not the entity is a 'partnership' as defined in Item 901(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual partnership supplements (Item 902) — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more entities are proposed in a roll-up transaction, a separate supplement for each entity must be provided containing specified disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each supplement (filed as part of the registration statement and delivered with the prospectus) must include: (1) a forepart statement that supplements have been prepared for each partnership, effects may differ, and that upon written request a copy will be transmitted promptly without charge (include name/address for requests); (2) a brief description of each material risk and effect of the roll-up (including federal income tax consequences) with cross-references to Items 904 and 915; (3) a statement whether the general partner reasonably believes the transaction is fair or unfair to investors and bases for the belief, with cross-references to Item 910 and description of material differences if any; (4) a brief narrative description of the method of calculating the value of the partnership and allocating interests in the successor, and a table showing such calculation and allocation including: (i) appraised value of each separately appraised significant asset or assigned values for assets without appraisals; (ii) dollar amount of mortgages/liabilities on each asset; (iii) cash and cash equivalents; (iv) other assets; (v) other liabilities; (vi) value assigned to partnership; (vii) value per interest (equivalent basis); (viii) aggregate number of interests in successor and percentage of total interests; (ix) number of interests in successor allocated to investors per interest held; (x) value assigned to general partner's interest and number of interests/consideration allocated as compensation/reimbursement; (5) amounts of compensation paid and cash distributions to general partner and affiliates for last three fiscal years and most recent interim period and amounts that would have been paid if successor's compensation/distribution structure had been in effect, and description of proposed changes that would materially change compensation; (6) cash distributions made to investors during each of last five fiscal years and most recent interim period identifying any representing return of capital; (7) appropriate cross-reference to selected financial information and pro forma financial statements included in the principal disclosure document (Item 914(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary requirements for roll-up disclosure (Item 903)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear, concise, comprehensible summary of the roll-up transaction in the forepart of the disclosure document and include specified summary items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary shall include: (1) each material risk and effect on investors, including changes in business plan, voting rights, cash distribution policies, form of ownership interest or management compensation; the general partner's conflicts of interest; and the likelihood that securities received will trade at prices substantially below values assigned; (2) material terms of the roll-up including the valuation method used to allocate securities in the successor; (3) whether the general partner reasonably believes the transaction is fair or unfair to investors with bases for such belief; (4) any outside opinion concerning fairness and contacts with outside parties concerning fairness opinions/valuations/reports required by Item 911(a)(5); (5) background and reasons for the roll-up and alternatives described in Item 908(b); (6) rights of investors to dissenters' or appraisal rights and to obtain a list of investors in the partnership; (7) if affiliates of the general partner or sponsor may participate in successor's business or receive compensation, include an organizational chart showing relationships among general partner, sponsor and affiliates. Instruction: The description of material risks and effects must be presented prominently in the forepart of the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk factors and other considerations (Item 904)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section header indicating risk factors and other considerations follow immediately after the summary required by Item 903.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The item begins 'Immediately following the summary required by Item 903...' (full text continues beyond this chunk). Present risk factors directly after the summary to inform investors of material risks and considerations.
